events.title: Summer on the Hudson: Art in the Park
events.description: Art in the Park invites children ages 3-8 to learn about their local environment through a mix of arts & crafts activities. This hands-on, place-based curriculum builds kids' appreciation for the plants, pollinators, and wildlife found in Riverside Park, and fosters their creativity. Mondays and Thursdays at Camel Playground; Tuesdays and Wednesdays at Hippo Playground. Art in the Park is fully funded by proceeds from the Hippo Playground Spring Fair.

events.title: Summer on the Hudson: Children's Performance Series featuring Arm-of-the-Sea Theatre
events.description: Music, storytelling, and theatre for young audiences up to age 7. Wear sunscreen. July 9: Musiquita | Joyful bilingual music for kids inspired by Latin folk traditions July 16: Lucy Kalantari & the Jazz Cats | Interactive swingin’ sounds and jazz age play July 23: Joanie Leeds | GRAMMY-winning singer-songwriter July 30: Arm of the Sea Theatre | presents "One Blue Sky”Arm-of-the-Sea is an arts ensemble that fuses visual storytelling with live music in large-scale works of mask and puppet theater. Founded in 1982 by Marlena Marallo and Patrick Wadden, the company’s hybrid performance style channels the evocative power of the arts as a force for joy, insight, and community uplift. Their low-tech devices of theatrical enchantment illuminate relations between humans and the life-support networks of this blue-ocean planet. Under the direction of Marallo & Wadden, the creative team includes musicians Maclain Maier, Joseph Davis & Helen Houghton; and performers Joanna Grabiarz, Doug Keller, DeeDee Maucher, Nick Panken, Rakel Stammer, Soyal Smalls and MJ Smythe.        Arm-of-the-Sea’s ONE BLUE SKY combines live music, puppet figures and visual poetry in a contemporary work of mask & puppet theater.  Mareesha is a young girl who undertakes a mythic journey to find her lost parent and discover her own powers. It is appropriate for ages 6 & up. Arm-of-the-Sea is an award-winning theater company currently in its 44th season. This production was made possible, in part, by a grant from the Jim Henson Foundation.  Arm-of-the-Sea tours its original productions to cultural centers, festivals, and community venues throughout New York and adjacent states. The organization is transforming the ruins of a 19th century papermill In Saugerties, NY into the Tidewater Center, a waterfront cultural park for bio-regional arts, environmental science & local heritage.Recent recognitions include: 2024 Hudson River Watershed Alliance “Wave-Makers” Award, 2018 Ulster County Executive's Arts Award for Arts Organization, a 2016 Environmental Champions Award from the US Environmental Protection Agency, the 2014 Excellence in Arts Award from Mill Street Loft, and the 2014 Distinguished Environmental Achievement Award from Mohonk Consultations. Directors Marallo & Wadden were 2013 Artists-in Residence at SUNY Ulster (Stone Ridge, NY), and 2014 Artists-in-Residence at the Cary Institute for Ecosystem Studies (Millbrook, NY).

events.title: Workshop for Volunteers: Building your Brand -- Visibility for Groups Dedicated to Parks
events.description: Is your grassroots organization trying to become more visible in your community? Are you interested in learning how to speak publicly about your group’s efforts? Join experts from TD as they walk through the basics of building your brand for small nonprofits and community-based organizations dedicated to local parks. You’ll have a chance to connect with other park supporters as well as members of TD’s Small Business team.In this workshop, you will:Learn branding basics for small nonprofits and community-based organizationsDraft and practice an elevator pitch Gain inspiration from examples of stellar grassroots groupsRegistration for this session is required and will close the day before the event. Questions? Reach out to academy@cityparksfoundation.org. At Partnerships for Parks, we help people, organizations, and government work together to support parks, gardens, trees, and other green and open spaces in New York City. Our free workshops are a great way to network and learn the skills needed to start, build, or sustain a community group dedicated to local green space.

events.title: Writers Workshop at Bryant Park Reading Room
events.description: Fiction is a conjuring act. The writer builds a bridge of words for the reader’s imagination to cross—a tricky collaboration, to be sure. Join us for a free workshop with Gotham Fiction instructor Susan Breen to get some grounded craft advice and work on your stories. Nothing beats playing make-believe on the page in the heart of summertime New York City.About the instructorSusan Breen is the author of the novels Merry (Alcove Press), The Fiction Class (Plume/Headline Review UK), and the Maggie Dove mystery series (originally published by Penguin Random House/Alibi and rereleased by Under the Oak Press). Her short stories have appeared in American Literary Review, the Chattahoochee Review, Alfred Hitchcock Mystery Magazine, and Ellery Queen’s Mystery Magazine, as well as the anthologies Best American Nonrequired Reading and Murder Most Diabolical, and she has won the Margery Allingham Short Mystery Competition. She holds a BA from the University of Rochester and an MA in Economics from Columbia University.

40 in Focus: SummerStage through the Lens of Photographer Jack Vartoogian
events.description: From 1987 to 2019, celebrated NYC photographer Jack Vartoogian captured hundreds of SummerStage performances across Manhattan parks, from Central Park to Marcus Garvey Park and Tompkins Square Park. This selection of intimate, rarely seen imagery gives viewers a look back at past decades of outdoor live music in New York City, a peek behind the curtain with never-before-seen backstage photos and honors those artists who have passed on. From the earliest performances with Sun Ra Arkestra and Mavis and Pop Staples, to legendary artists in memoriam like Tito Puente and Hugh Masekela and backstage shots of Buddy Guy and Darlene Love, this exhibition celebrates not only a photographer’s commitment to documenting performance but also celebrates a 40-year legacy of SummerStage.This free exhibition is presented by City Parks Foundation in collaboration with NYC Parks Art & Antiquities department.An opening reception will be held on June 16 from 6pm-8 pm, offering light refreshments, music and an exclusive exhibition poster while supplies last. Image credit: Sun Ra Arkestra at SummerStage, 1989, Jack Vartoogian
